subtype: Approach: jumping into the deep end to prove he is brave [Pitfall]
passage: At the municipal pool in Valencia, Yosef watched Santiago and two others dare each other at the edge. "Bet you won't jump in the deep end," Santiago said. The coach had gone inside for a whistle. Yosef, who could only manage the shallow lanes, took a breath and jumped. The cold closed over his head. He kicked, swallowed a mouthful of water and could not find the bottom. Santiago shouted for help. The lifeguard dived in and hauled him to the wall while he coughed. Later, wrapped in a towel, Yosef listened as the coach spoke to the whole group. His legs still shook. He had wanted to look brave; now he only wanted to learn properly.

qa.a: He jumped into the deep end of the pool.

qa.q: What was Yosef feeling as he sat wrapped in the towel?
qa.a: Shaky and scared, and a little ashamed, since he wanted to look brave but now only wants to learn properly.

qa.q: What could Yosef have done when Santiago dared him?
qa.a: He could have said no and asked the coach for a lesson, because being brave can mean choosing to learn safely.

qa.q: How might the lifeguard see what happened?
qa.a: The lifeguard sees a child in trouble in water too deep for his skill and acts at once, so the focus is on getting him out safely.

grounding: A boy jumps into the deep pool without the coach to prove he is brave, panics, is pulled out and learns skill matters.

subtype: Approach: jumping into the deep end to prove he is brave [Pitfall]
passage: At the sports club pool, the beginners had to stay in the shallow end until the coach said otherwise. But on Friday the coach was late, and some older boys were jumping off the deep-end block. "Come on, Varun, you're not scared, are you?" Varun climbed up. He jumped. The water closed over his head, and he couldn't find the bottom or the top. He thrashed, swallowed water. Rekha, the lifeguard, was already in the water. She hooked him under the arms and pulled him to the side. He clung to the edge, coughing, shaking. When the coach arrived, he sat with Varun on the bench. "Brave is doing it when you're ready, with me here," he said. Varun nodded, still shaking.

qa.q: Who pulled Varun to the side?
qa.a: Rekha, the lifeguard, pulled him to the side.

qa.q: How did Varun feel clinging to the edge?
qa.a: He was frightened and shaken, coughing and shaking after the panic.

qa.q: What should Varun do next time the older boys tease him, and why?
qa.a: Stay in the shallow end and wait for the coach, because saying no to a dare is safer than trying something he can't yet do.

qa.q: How does the jump look to Rekha, the lifeguard?
qa.a: Rekha sees a beginner in danger and acts at once, and she is probably worried and relieved it ended safely.

grounding: It shows a boy jumping into the deep pool without the coach to prove he is brave, panicking and needing to be pulled out.

subtype: Approach: jumping into the deep end to prove he is brave [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Gautam, and I was there when Francis jumped into the deep end of the swimming pool at the club in Panaji. He'd only had four lessons. The coach had gone to the office for a minute, and one of the older boys dared him. Francis looked at the water for a long time. Then he jumped. He didn't come up properly. His arms were slapping the water and his face kept going under. I yelled for help, and the lifeguard dived in and pulled him out. The coach ran back. Francis sat wrapped in a towel, very quiet. The coach talked to him for a long time, and then called his mother. I don't know if he was more scared or more embarrassed. Probably both.

qa.q: How many lessons had Francis had?
qa.a: He had only had four lessons.

qa.q: What might Francis have been feeling, sitting wrapped in a towel?
qa.a: He may have been both scared and embarrassed, though Gautam can only guess from how quiet he was.

qa.q: What could the club change to stop this happening again?
qa.a: The club could make sure beginners are never left at the pool without a coach or lifeguard watching them, and ban dares.

qa.q: How does the jump look to Francis's coach?
qa.a: The coach sees a beginner put in danger during a short absence and takes it seriously, talking to Francis and calling his mother.

grounding: It shows a boy jumping into the deep end without the coach to seem brave, panicking and being pulled out.
